critique.summary: The requested headline copy change is applied ("Calmer clinics, faster triage" is visible), but the surrounding poster is broken on multiple axes: the hero "image" is a gratuitous blue-to-purple/green gradient with a nebulous glowing orb (a textbook AI-cliche placeholder, not credible imagery), there is a large dead band between the headline and the body line, the text is hard-margin-flush to the left edge (no left padding on the band), and there is a wide unused top margin above the hero. The result reads as an unfinished poster with a placeholder image, not a shippable hero.

issues.message: The hero image is a generic blue/green/purple gradient with a soft glowing orb — a stock AI-cliche visual that carries no editorial meaning for a 'Case Study: calmer clinics, faster triage' hero. Fails the imagery RELEVANCE gate and reads as a placeholder.
issues.suggested_repair: Replace the hero asset with a purposeful editorial photograph (e.g. a calm clinic reception / clinician on a call) via asset(action="generate_image", target_node_id="hero"), or drop the image and use the typographic Idiom B (solid brand band). Do NOT keep the gradient-orb placeholder.

issues.message: Large dead vertical band between the headline 'Calmer clinics, faster triage' and the body line 'How Insight Health cut phone wait times…' — roughly ~150pt of empty space with nothing in it, making the poster read unfinished.
issues.suggested_repair: Tighten the band's inter-item gap to $space.stack.default (or reduce the kicker→headline→body gaps) so the three text lines read as one coherent stack, and let the outer artboard absorb the slack with a fill-height main region (y(c)).

issues.message: The kicker, headline, and body text are flush to the left edge of the page (x≈0) with no left padding. The hero image also sits flush to the very edges. There is no consistent outer margin — the poster has no framed content column.
issues.suggested_repair: Give the artboard/canvas pad(64) (or the band its own pad) so the text sits in a consistent inset column and the hero image aligns to the same margin (or is deliberately full-bleed while text stays inset).

issues.message: There is a noticeable empty band above the hero image at the top of the page while the text sits low; distribution is uneven top-to-bottom.
issues.suggested_repair: Either make the hero full-bleed to the top edge (p(0,0)) or wrap the content in a y(s)/y(c) auto-layout with consistent section gaps so the top margin matches the outer padding.

issues.message: On a 1080×1350 poster the headline reads at roughly A4 scale — it does not clearly dominate relative to the huge hero image band above it. Squint test: the gradient orb pulls the eye more than the headline.
issues.suggested_repair: Step the headline size up with font_size($type.size.6xl) or 7xl so it dominates the poster; keep style($type.headline) for weight/color.

critique.repair_instruction: Replace the placeholder gradient/orb hero image with a purposeful editorial photo relevant to 'calmer clinics, faster triage' (or drop the image entirely and use the solid brand-band Idiom B); add consistent outer padding (pad(64)) to the artboard/band so text is not flush to the left edge; tighten the vertical gaps in the text band so headline/kicker/body read as one coherent stack with no dead band between them; and step the headline size up to $type.size.6xl or 7xl so it clearly dominates the 1080×1350 canvas.
requirement_coverage_notes: Headline text now reads 'Calmer clinics, faster triage' — the user's requested copy change is present.
User asked to 'keep everything else exactly as it is', but the surrounding layout still fails visual quality gates independent of that request; noting the failures for the coordinator.
